S88.01.needs: none (an internet connection to open the docs page)
S88.01.note: This is the only per-screen help link found in the VS Code app. The Help menu's Documentation item opens the general docs page. The configuration and custom-instructions articles (apps/web/content/support) are not linked from the VS Code app. I did not check when the onboarding screen is shown.
steps: Open the AGI Code sidebar and go to the onboarding screen that has the Permission docs link.
Click Permission docs.
Look at the browser that opens: it should be the docs page for permissions (URL contains topic=permissions), and the article should explain the permission settings shown on that screen.

S88.04.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account (signed-out users get a Sign in prompt)
S88.04.note: The sidebar More actions button was located from its markup (title More, aria-label More actions) but its visible position was not confirmed. The build and platform are added to the sent report silently, so the tester cannot see them in the UI.
steps: Open the Command Palette and type Code: Send Feedback, or open the sidebar's More actions menu and choose Help > Send feedback.
Pick Report a Bug from the list.
Type a description in the box that reads Report a Bug: Describe your feedback, then press Enter.
Look for the notification that says your feedback reached the team. Compare with Expected: the form asks only for text, and the build and platform are sent with the report without being shown to you.
S88.04.where: Command palette > Code: Send Feedback > Report a Bug (also Sidebar > More actions > Help > Send feedback)

S88.05.note: The tester cannot see the stored record from inside the app; the code sends it to the server endpoint /api/feedback and labels it as general feedback.
steps: Open the Command Palette and type Code: Send Feedback.
Pick General Feedback (description: Share thoughts about the extension).
Type a message in the box and press Enter.
Look for the notification that says your feedback reached the team. Compare with Expected.
S88.05.where: Command palette > Code: Send Feedback > General Feedback

S88.06.note: The request is stored on the server as a feature-type report, which the tester cannot see from the app.
steps: Open the Command Palette and type Code: Send Feedback.
Pick Feature Request (description: Suggest a new feature or improvement).
Type the request in the box and press Enter.
Look for the notification that says your feedback reached the team. Compare with Expected.
S88.06.where: Command palette > Code: Send Feedback > Feature Request

S88.07.note: The Expected line says the user can see what the bundle contains and choose to share it. The code only offers a save dialog after the server redacts the bundle; sharing with support is a manual step, and the Help item's description reads: A redacted report to attach when you contact support.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud (signed-out, the command shows a message and exports nothing).
Open the Command Palette and type Code: Export Diagnostics, or use Help > Export diagnostics from the sidebar's More actions menu.
Wait for the save dialog to open, then save the JSON file somewhere you choose.

Open the saved file and check its fields (for example collectedAt, surface, appVersion, platform, locale, recentEvents), then compare with Expected. Note the save dialog is the only point of choice: there is no preview in the app and no share-with-support button, so the tester attaches the file to support by hand. Cancelling the dialog writes nothing.
S88.07.where: Command palette > Code: Export Diagnostics (also Sidebar > More actions > Help > Export diagnostics)

S88.08.needs: a request that fails with a server failure (not controllable from the app)
S88.08.note: The reference is shown only when the failure carries a requestId and the turn failure is the typed kind. A failure without that id shows no reference. I did not confirm that the reference text can be copied, and I could not find a way to trigger a failure on demand.
steps: Send a chat message in the AGI Code sidebar.
Make the request fail (this cannot be set up on demand; it needs a failing request that the server answers with a typed failure).
Read the error message in the chat. It should end with Reference: followed by an id.
Copy the id and compare with Expected: the id must be one the user can quote to support.
S88.08.where: Sidebar chat > a message that fails > error message (the Reference: line)
